preamble: The open-mid back unrounded [ʌ] centralizes to schwa [ə] in two ways in English. Monosyllabic function words with STRUT in their strong form (but, us, must, some) have weak forms with [ə] when unstressed. In Welsh English the STRUT vowel itself is a mid-central [ɜ~ə] even under stress, so STRUT and schwa are close or merged.

examples.note: The weak form is used whenever the word is unstressed, and the strong form under contrastive stress.
Wiktionary records South Welsh but as /ˈbət/ (strut–comma merger).

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Weak and strong forms in English. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weak_and_strong_forms_in_English
